item.research_question: How does chemical short-range order (SRO) affect the mobility mechanisms of screw and edge dislocations in the MoNbTaW refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) across a wide temperature range?
item.material_system: MoNbTaW refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA), specifically comparing random solid solution (RSS) and equilibrium SRO states at 800 K
item.processing_route: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations using a moment tensor potential (MTP) machine-learning interatomic potential; SRO states equilibrated via hybrid MD/Monte Carlo (MD/MC) approach at 800 K
item.test_conditions: Temperatures from 300 K to 2000 K; applied shear stresses ranging from 0 to 3.0 GPa for screws and 0 to 1.0 GPa for edges; dislocation line length ~15 nm
key_findings: At 300 K, SRO provides an extra strengthening of ~180 MPa for screw dislocations due to the formation of diffuse antiphase boundaries (DAPBs).
The strengthening effect of SRO on screw dislocations attenuates with increasing temperature, becoming negligible at 2000 K where mobility curves for RSS and SRO samples overlap.
A cross-slip locking mechanism involving the formation of jogs is observed for screw dislocations, providing extra strengthening independent of SRO presence.
Unlike screw dislocations, the mobility of edge dislocations is enhanced by the presence of SRO, particularly in the high-stress regime.
The SRO-induced enhancement of edge dislocation mobility extends to a characteristic length scale of approximately 1.2 nm into neighboring planes.
At 300 K, dislocation velocities in the MoNbTaW RHEA are significantly lower than in pure Mo and Nb, but this difference diminishes at 2000 K.
The attenuation of SRO strengthening at high temperatures is attributed to the increasing contribution of the entropy term (ΔS_kp) to the kink-pair formation free energy.
item.mechanism: For screw dislocations, SRO creates an energy barrier (DAPB formation energy) that must be overcome during kink-pair nucleation, causing strengthening that is thermally activated and thus diminishes at high temperatures. For edge dislocations, SRO flattens the energy landscape, reducing solute drag effects and enhancing mobility despite the energy cost of disrupting order on the slip plane. Cross-slip locking in screws involves the formation of jogs on different slip planes that pin the dislocation line.
item.limitations: The simulations use short dislocation line lengths (~15 nm) compared to realistic experimental conditions, meaning calculated velocities are dependent on this size and cannot be directly compared to macroscopic theoretical models without extrapolation. The study assumes the SRO state remains fixed during dislocation motion and does not account for changes in ordering around the moving core.
item.future_work: The authors state that predicting how the identified mechanisms combine to determine material strength requires appealing to mesoscale models for longer dislocation lengths and longer timescales, which is beyond the scope of the current work.
quotes: The mobility of edge dislocations is found to be enhanced by the presence of SRO, whereas the rate of double-kink nucleation in the motion of screw dislocations is reduced.
At 300 K (Fig. 2c), the influence of SRO is clearly apparent; based on the shift in the velocity curve, we can estimate the extra strengthening from SRO to be ~180 MPa.
This result supports our hypothesis that SRO would reduce the solute drag interaction for the edge dislocation, and shows that this effect extends to a characteristic length scale of ~1.2 nm.

item.research_question: How does chemical short-range order (SRO) and temperature affect the mobility and friction stress of edge versus screw dislocations in a bcc MoNbTaW refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) compared to pure bcc metals and binary alloys?
item.material_system: MoNbTaW refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA), pure Mo, and binary Mo-Nb alloys (Mo95Nb5 to Mo75Nb25)
item.processing_route: Machine-learning interatomic potential (MTP) with radius cutoff (Rcut) of 4.7 Å and maximum level (levmax) of 14; MC/MD equilibration at 800 K; dislocation mobility simulations using LAMMPS with shear stress ramped at 20 MPa per 1.5 ps and held for 150 ps at temperatures of 300 K and 2000 K
item.test_conditions: Temperatures: 300 K and 2000 K; Shear stress ramp rate: 20 MPa per 1.5 ps; Hold time: 150 ps; Critical friction stress defined at 0.2 Å/ps for screw and 1.0 Å/ps for edge dislocations
key_findings: The edge-to-screw velocity ratio decreases from 20 at 300 K to 11 at 2000 K in MoNbTaW.
Critical friction stress for edge dislocations decreases by 140 MPa from 300 to 2000 K.
Critical friction stress for screw dislocations decreases by 1.3 GPa (an order of magnitude larger) from 300 to 2000 K.
At ~2000 K, the critical friction stresses for both edge and screw dislocations decay to approximately the same level.
SRO hinders screw dislocation motion but accelerates edge dislocation motion in the RHEA.
A novel cross-slip locking mechanism was observed in the RHEA, attributed to intrinsic energy fluctuations and rugged energy landscapes.
Critical stress for screw dislocations follows an exponential decay with temperature, while edge dislocations follow a linear decrease.
Binary Mo-Nb alloys show lower critical friction stresses compared to the RHEA, with edge friction converging to zero in pure bcc metals.
item.mechanism: Screw dislocations move via kink-pair nucleation and migration; SRO increases the free-energy barrier for kink-pair nucleation, causing temperature-dependent strengthening. Edge dislocations are accelerated by SRO through the attenuation of solute interaction magnitudes. The cross-slip locking mechanism arises from intrinsic energy fluctuations along the dislocation line and the rugged energy landscape.
item.limitations: The study notes that the cross-slip locking mechanism was observed even with a limited cell size, implying potential size effects, and the phenomenological model is constructed specifically for the double-kink mechanism.
item.future_work: The authors state that the findings demonstrate mechanisms that can have a significant impact on mechanical properties, implying future work should explore these impacts, though no specific future experiments are explicitly detailed in the provided text.
quotes: The edge-to-screw mobility ratio is around 20 at 300 K, which decreases to 11 when the temperature is raised to 2000 K.
Short-range order (SRO) is found to play opposite roles in the motion of screw and edge dislocation in RHEAs: it will hinder screw dislocation motion yet accelerate the motion of edges.
From 300 to 2000 K the critical friction stress decreases by 140 MPa for the edge dislocation, whereas the decrease is almost an order of magnitude larger at 1.3 GPa for the screw dislocation.
